text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The United Nations sees an alignment of views on the Cyprus dispute between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides, while the United States once again raises the issue of a ban on military overflights.
- Former justice minister Alecos Evangelou accused political parties of trying to promote nepotism in the police force during his term in office.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash calls President Glafcos Clerides to talks.
- Former justice minister Evangelou lashes out at the "interference" of Democratic Party leader and House speaker Spyros Kyprianou.
- Reactions continue after cabinet reshuffle. (Right-wing) Democratic Rally members say Clerides did not consult them about the shakeup.

- The pressure is on in opposition parties to find a common candidate for the presidential elections. Socialist Edek party leader Vassos Lyssarides warns other opposition parties the delay may lead to failure.
- Ministers depart from the government with bitterness. Outgoing foreign minister Alecos Michaelides did not say one "thank you" in his farewell speech.
- More military exercises with Greece are planned within the framework of the joint defence pact.
